documented_requirements.requirement: Spanish is a supported Merchant language. Supported languages can target supported countries; the United States supports USD and free listings. Data and buyer-facing currency must remain consistent; country shipping data uses the submitted product currency.
Keep the same stable offer ID for the same product across languages within a country. Different variants require their own IDs; language expansion is not a reason to invent replacement offer IDs.

Within an account, current Merchant product identity combines contentLanguage, feedLabel and offerId, rendered logically as contentLanguage~feedLabel~offerId. Legacy Content API examples include channel; that legacy representation must not replace the current logical key.

For a file primary source, contentLanguage and feedLabel are both required and immutable; it accepts that combination. Content language uses two-letter ISO639-1. Target countries and marketing destinations are separate settings. Unrestricted-language API-source examples do not relax the file-source constraint.

Google warns against supplying the same ID/language/feed-label combination through multiple sources. Merchant API migration documentation explains that inserting the same key into another primary source can transfer ownership from the prior source; do not assume a particular collision error or transfer result for this account's file workflow.

Product data and key landing-page elements should match the selected language. A majority mismatch may cause disapproval; other key mismatches may limit performance. Checkout navigation and information needed to decide a purchase must use the feed language. Relevant pages include cart, checkout, Terms, refund/return policy, and About/contact information.

The linked live product page must show the same product/variant, matching price, currency and availability, with a usable buying route and the claimed domain. A locale-looking URL does not prove compliance. Google lists default selection of the matching variant as a best practice, distinct from the minimum product-match requirements.

Google accepts TXT, XML and TSV product files up to4GB. Direct manual upload does not synchronize later file changes; each changed file needs resubmission. The content/format must satisfy the product-data specification.

A scheduled source uses a direct, accessible HTTP/HTTPS/SFTP file URL and permissions that let Google retrieve it. Google documents a24-hour default, adjustable schedule. That default does not verify the actual account schedule, endpoint durability, successful fetch or local lifecycle freshness.

The Products API guide advises refresh at least every30days to prevent expiration; this is not an allowance to leave changed product data stale or override stricter local deadlines. Upload/processing is followed by product completeness/policy review; receipt success alone does not certify approval or serving.

derived_conditions.condition: For the same verified feed label and existing offer ID, es and en produce distinct logical product keys. Use the existing stable US product/variant IDs, not fabricated Spanish ID suffixes. No actual feed label, product key or new source ID is selected in this review.

The owner first qualifies any already-existing Spanish primary source/product keys, country targets, rules and input method. If none exists, only a separately reviewed Spanish file source can be proposed; uploading Spanish content into the English source or creating a duplicate Spanish key is not a safe language-isolation plan.

Preserve the existing English source identity, rows, rules and delivery configuration. File-source creation or upload requires the parent's exact later release decision. This documentation review grants neither source-write nor paid authority.

material_failure_conditions: Identical full language/feed-label/offer-ID key already owned by a different source, or a mismatched source language/label.
Predominantly wrong-language product data, buyer-decision information or checkout that falls back to English, or unverified Spanish variants.
Wrong product/variant, unavailable buying route, broken/unclaimed-domain landing link, or price/currency/availability disagreement.
Unsupported/malformed/oversize file, unreadable scheduled endpoint, failed fetch, or manual data allowed to become stale.

Source processing success treated as whole-cohort approval, current English preservation assumed without a receiving comparison, or new-source defaults treated as proof of free-listings-only destinations.
account_facts_not_verified: Any current US/es source or product-key inventory, including automatic sources, and which exact source owns each full key.
Actual existing feed label, source ID, editable native controls, quotas/permissions, destination participation, and input method.
Spanish data completeness and actual Spanish US/USD landing/cart/checkout/Terms/refund/contact presentation.
Current product/variant availability, holds, price/shipping truth, approved offer counts or receiving results.
Actual fetch timing, hostname durability or operational freshness; no endpoint/network checks were run.
bounded_next_step: Existing Merchant owner completes its already-dispatched read-only US/es source-key inventory and Spanish buyer-path qualification, then freezes one exact candidate/source plan for parent review. No submission is authorized by this report.
